cards.text: This one's a song for the choirmaster, played on stringed instruments. The singers keep saying "us," and they open with a big ask: "May God be gracious to us and bless us." Then they ask Him to "cause His face to shine upon us."

cards.question: True or false: when the singers ask God to make His face shine on them, they're asking Him to look on them with kindness.

cards.text: After a Selah, the singers say WHY they want all that blessing. Me, fresh out of the junk drawer? I'd have asked for a bigger oven and a REALLY long nap.

cards.question: Why do the singers want God to bless them?

answers.text: So His ways are known on earth
So their land is safe from war
So they can rest from hard work

cards.question: True or false: the singers want God's salvation known only among their own people.

cards.text: They ask for a blessing so the WHOLE EARTH can know God's ways. That's like asking for one cookie so you can feed the whole block, and then the song breaks into a chorus.

cards.question: The chorus calls on someone to praise God. Who?

cards.text: Next they say, "Let the nations be glad and sing for joy," and they give a reason. Joy for EVERY nation, friend, and I get excited when a batch comes out not burnt.

cards.question: Why should the nations be glad and sing for joy?
The singers say God judges the peoples justly and ___ the nations of the earth.

cards.text: After another Selah, that chorus comes right back: "Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You." Word for word, and I'd sing it twice too, but trust me, NOBODY wants to hear me sing it twice.
Then the song stops asking and looks down at the ground. Something good has come up out of the earth.

cards.question: True or false: the song opened asking God to bless the singers, and now they say God, their God, blesses them.

cards.text: One last line, and the blessing shows up one more time. And then, friend, the singers say what it's for.

cards.question: God blesses the singers so that who will fear Him?

answers.text: All the ends of the earth

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "May God be gracious to us and bless us.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "cause His face to shine upon us.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The first sentence only restates verse 2, which cards 4 and 5 already covered (the blessing is so God's ways are known on earth, among all nations). It is a recap, not a new moment. The card's only new beat is 'the song breaks into a chorus,' tacked onto the end of the joke sentence.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank copies verse 4's line word for word and blanks its next word ('leads'). The baker is guessing the line's wording, which they haven't seen, rather than reasoning out meaning. Card 9 already asked about the reason in this same line.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup says 'Something good has come up out of the earth.' That rules out both wrong answers on card 13 ('thorns' and 'dust'), so only 'harvest' is left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'The earth has yielded its ___.' is verse 6's opening line word for word, with its last word blanked. The baker is asked to guess the next word of a line, not something about the passage's movement or meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
